payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Use only the saved statuses and image-grounded evidence from n1 and n2. complete: both supports pass, establishing both a chalk medium and a drawing. partial: at least one support passes, but the other fails, so some requested transformation is evidenced without complete fulfillment. absent: both supports fail, establishing neither requested feature. unknown: no support passes and at least one is unknown, leaving progress unresolved. A known failure is negative evidence, not uncertainty; do not infer facts beyond the support evidence. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk. Combine the independent evidence for chalk medium and drawing form; do not inspect images or add requirements.

node_traces.evidence: Both saved support observations pass: n1 establishes a chalk-like medium, and n2 establishes a drawn rather than photographic form. Together they support the requested chalk drawing transformation.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image has a visibly grainy, smudged surface and soft, chalk-like strokes across the scene, consistent with a chalk drawing treatment.
The edited image visibly renders the giraffes and surroundings with softened, sketch-like drawn contours and shading rather than retaining the source photograph's photographic appearance.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s rule maps two passing supports directly to complete, but the edited image shows a mixed result: it has chalk-like grain and smudging, while the giraffes and scene retain substantial photographic detail and contrast rather than reading clearly as a drawing. The support evidence is therefore too permissive, especially n2’s inference from softened contours to a drawn form. Tighten the evidence standard for each support to distinguish a convincing chalk drawing from a photo with a chalk-like filter, and ensure the aggregate preserves partial progress when only one requested aspect is convincingly established. Keep the decision grounded in the saved evidence and image; do not treat high confidence or agreement between correlated visual cues as proof of completion. There are no transport, schema, or dependency failures here: both supports executed successfully, so the issue is semantic calibration, not missing evidence."}
